rationale: Both cards are the one thing a parent does to rein Happy in, texting it to stop (or to show its state), at two scopes, and the installed code shows the overlap is larger than either card or the purpose passes of rounds 3 and 4 recorded: the built-in stop is not only `/stop` but any message that consists solely of one of a fixed list of 43 stop phrases, among them 'stop', 'please stop', 'stop openclaw', '停止' and '暂停' (dist/abort-trigger-text-lTiWnvSe.mjs, mentioned in docs/web/control-ui/chat.md:353), and that check runs in the common inbound path before any plugin `before_dispatch` hook (dist/dispatch-from-config-BfxY-Rlw.mjs, where prepareDispatchOperation precedes chooseDispatchRoute; read from the bundled code, not tried on iMessage), so 'stop by text' in plain words already exists for one answer in one chat, G005's in-house phrase is its second level and has to be worded around that built-in list, and the single paper sheet from which parents learn the words (G005 keeps its phrases out of Happy's help text, and that sheet is the only thing OCL-06 builds) has to say which words end one answer and which stop everything. Rounds 3 and 4 proposed the pair without this fact and it was not taken up, with no verdict in either history; no rule above is crossed, because both are wave A and low risk on the same parents' threads, neither adds a tool, a recipient or a data source, and the merged card states its two parts separately (what works today with nothing to build: the built-in commands and stop words, with Tony's one choice about leaving /restart and /update reachable from chat; and what needs the in-house plugin: the stop-everything and lock-out phrases), while mute and vacation mode stay with the notification policy (G001) and the recovery card (CRT-05) stays apart because of its envelope decision.
name: Stopping and checking Happy by text: the built-in commands and stop words (/stop or a bare 'stop', /new, /status, /usage, /tools), then 'Happy, stop everything' and locking one person out
